newsitem.title: USA: U.S. proposes world trade ban on Mexican parrots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. proposes world trade ban on Mexican parrots.

text.p: The United States proposed on Friday to ban all international trade in two Mexican parrot species and sawfish to help save them from extinction, and sought restrictions in mahogany trade.

The proposals were submitted to the secretariat of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES), the world's broadest conservation agreement, ahead of a biennial meeting in Zimbabwe in June.
The proposed ban on trade in green-cheeked parrots and yellow-headed parrots, both popular as pets, is being supported by Mexico.
Sawfish, related to sharks and known for their long saw-like snouts, are threatened with extinction because they are caught as tourist curios, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service said.

Along with bigleaf mahogany, the United States proposed to impose controls on trade of goldenseal, a North American medicinal plant, map turtles, the alligator snapping trule, the timber rattlesnake, and the straw-headed bulbul.
The turtles and the bulbul, a bird, are generally exported as pets. The rattlesnake is exported for its leather and as a food product.

The Fish and Wildlife Service said listing of bigleaf mahogany timber for import and export controls, a move supported by Bolivia, the second largest exporter, would not affect trade in furniture or other products.
"It will help ensure that mahogany entering the United States was harvested in a sustainable way and comes from legal sources," said Fish and Wildlife Service Director John Rogers.
The United States is the biggest consumer of bigleaf mahogany.
